summary: VERIFY round. The delta claim is proven exactly, not merely plausible: reconstructing the previous staged tree by swapping blob 24bfeec5 (11 @Test) back in for buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/CoverageGateTest.java and rehashing `git diff --cached` reproduces 6518cbe64dfb4657d3b094b1603ebb8e46267fed36b4334b59586c35b644fa46 -- the hash of the last recorded reviewer verdict. No production byte changed; the only delta is that one test file, 11 -> 13 methods (blob 90ca549). The two new tests assert behaviour coverage.py already had, and the pass/fail behaviour they lock in is correct: a branch-free module must not fail a branch floor, and buildSrc must not fail the gate. What is wrong is narrower and all latent -- the gate's summary line can state a success that is false, and 'no counter' is displayed as a measured 100%. Nothing here changes an exit status on the current tree, and the gate is unwired, so all findings are minor. No object-store request is introduced or altered by any file in this diff; the only new cost is a Gradle run per invocation of an unwired gate, already scoped to M0.39.

findings.title: A baselined module is counted as 'meeting' the floors, so the summary line reports a success that did not happen
findings.location: scripts/coverage.py, main(): `measured += 1` executes before `if m in skips:`
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced in a scratch tree: a module at line 10.0% / branch 10.0% listed in baselines/coverage.txt makes the gate print `WARN format ... EXCLUDED: needs work` and then, as its final line, `ok   1 module(s) meet 95% line / 90% branch`. Zero modules meet the floors. With every module baselined it would print `ok 8 module(s) meet 95% line / 90% branch` while enforcing nothing on anything -- the exact defect this file's own docstring says it exists to prevent, and it gets louder as testing.md rule 7's 'growing file' grows. The exit status stays 0, which is correct for an exclusion, so only the sentence lies. Minor only because baselines/coverage.txt does not exist in this tree, so `skips` is always empty and the branch is currently unreachable; it becomes live the first time anyone adds an exclusion. Fix is one line: count exclusions separately, or increment `measured` after the `skips` check.

findings.title: pct() cannot distinguish 'nothing to cover' from 'nothing was measured', and the new test cements that for both dimensions
findings.location: scripts/coverage.py, pct() and the two `c.get(..., (0, 0))` call sites in main()
findings.failure_scenario: For BRANCH the answer the new test asserts is right -- a records-only module has no branches, so no branch can be missed, and failing it against a 90% floor would be wrong. But the gate then prints `branch 100.0% (floor 90)`, which in a log is indistinguishable from a module with 400 fully covered branches; when check-mutants.sh lands in M0.14 and reports a poor kill rate on that module, the coverage line will have said 100%. Printing `n/a` when total == 0 costs one word, and aReportWithNoBranchCounterScoresFullBranchCoverage would still pass -- it asserts only exit 0 and no traceback, so it does not block the fix. The asymmetry is the sharper half: the same `(0, 0)` default is applied to LINE, where an absent counter never means 'nothing to cover'. Any JaCoCo report that analysed a class emits a LINE counter, so LINE missing means the measurement is broken, and the gate would print `ok line 100.0%` for it. The `c == {}` guard catches only the case where every counter is absent, not a partially-populated report (e.g. one carrying CLASS/METHOD but no LINE, as a merge or an over-broad jacoco `excludes` could produce). I did not demonstrate a JaCoCo version that emits such a report, so this is a robustness gap rather than a live bug -- but `if 'LINE' not in c: fail` is the one line that makes the two dimensions mean different things, and after this commit the shared permissive default reads as deliberate for both.

findings.title: The buildSrc filter is inert on the real tree, and the test's stated rationale for it is false
findings.location: scripts/coverage.py, main(): `not p.startswith('buildSrc/')`; buildSrcIsNotTreatedAsAProductModule in CoverageGateTest.java
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on this tree: removing the buildSrc/ filter and re-running the module selection yields buildSrc with has_classes = False, because buildSrc's main sources are Kotlin (binjava.java-conventions.gradle.kts, DependencyLicensesTask.kt, UpdateShasTask.kt) and compile to buildSrc/build/classes/kotlin/main, which the `build/classes/java/main/**/*.class` glob never looks at. It has no java/main directory at all. So the filter changes nothing today, and the test's comment -- 'Drop the buildSrc/ exclusion and the gate ... fails EVERY commit, docs-only included' -- does not hold for the real repository; the test only makes it hold by fabricating buildSrc/build/classes/java/main/binjava/X.class, a path buildSrc does not produce. The filter matters in the opposite direction from the one claimed: if buildSrc ever gains Java main sources, it silently exempts them from the only coverage floor this project has, at precisely the moment buildSrc's own build.gradle.kts says 'buildSrc holds real logic now ... so it gets tests like anything else'. And it is a hardcoded blanket exclusion that prints nothing -- the new test asserts doesNotContain("buildSrc") -- where a baselines/coverage.txt entry would print `WARN ... EXCLUDED: <reason>`. testing.md rule 7 says exclusions are named and justified, never blanket. Either express it as a baseline line so it is visible and reasoned, or derive the module list so buildSrc is simply not a module (see next finding), which needs no exclusion at all.

findings.title: The module list is a fourth independent derivation of a fact settings.gradle.kts already owns
findings.location: scripts/coverage.py, main(): `git ls-files '*/build.gradle.kts'` filtered by `p.count('/') == 1`, and the `build/classes/java/main` glob
findings.failure_scenario: check-module.sh has derive_modules(), a `modules` subcommand, and a comment at line 203 reading 'Derived from settings.gradle.kts, never restated. As a third hardcoded copy...' -- and three buildSrc suites (ModuleListDerivationTest, ModuleDriftTest, ModuleSelectionTest) exist to keep it honest. coverage.py restates it a fourth time with different rules, and nothing compares the two. I verified the two lists agree today (8 modules). They diverge on the first module that is not exactly one directory deep: a nested `plugin/consumer/build.gradle.kts` is in settings.gradle.kts, is built, has classes, and is silently dropped by `count('/') == 1` -- the gate prints `ok 8 module(s) meet ...` for a tree with nine, which is a green line over an unmeasured module. The inverse also silently misfires: a tracked top-level build.gradle.kts that is NOT in settings.gradle.kts becomes a module the gate demands a report for and Gradle never builds one, failing every commit. gate-design rung 2 is 'derive it from a source of truth' and this repository already built that source of truth; calling `./scripts/check-module.sh modules` would make the buildSrc special case disappear as a side effect. Related and in the same spirit: has_classes only globs build/classes/java/main, so a module whose main output lands anywhere else (Kotlin, an added source set, a multi-release layout) is `continue`d as 'nothing to cover yet' rather than reported. That is already true of buildSrc's Kotlin output today and would be true of any product module the day one stops being pure Java.
